_what: Settings for harness/wake-handlers/wake-stopped-chats.mjs, the part of the person's computer helper that wakes AI chats which stopped before their turn finished (a usage limit, an outage, a crash, the computer restarting or losing power) so nobody has to notice and start them again by hand. Every check_every_minutes it reads the transcripts touched in the last look_back_hours. A chat is judged by the last row of its turn (`turn_row`): the first of `rows` whose tests all hold (each test is { path, equals | one_of | present | starts_with }) says it finished, or that it stopped and why, and when it may go on (`resumes_at`, or wait_minutes after it stopped). A chat and all of its lanes must have been quiet for quiet_minutes (measured from each one's last turn row, not the file's mtime, which queued messages move), so a live chat is never woken. Each stop is handed out once through the person's Trillion (POST /handoffs, once_per the stop), one job per chat and one per stopped lane, never relaunched all at once from one place: the computer's taker (take-open-work.json max_concurrent) and other chats calling take_work pick them up a few at a time, because one chat relaunching about 80 lanes filled this computer's memory (84 GB, swap full) on 2026-10-04. A lane whose name has a newer transcript anywhere was already carried on and is left alone. A chat with a `live` block is also read from the computer's live status files (one per running process): a session that is busy is never handed out, and one waiting on a prompt nobody can answer is handed out at once as stuck, with no AI preferred. Messages waiting in a chat are counted by its `queued` rule and named in the job. Adding an AI is a row in `chats`; every word the AIs and the person read is here.
_stopped_chat_silence_minutes: The silence window a stopped chat's job keeps for that chat (src/agents.mjs anyoneFrom, chat_silence_minutes on the arrival). A stopped chat keeps no turn of its own, so it is 0: a chat not hosted here is open to any AI at once, and one hosted here is given back to itself first for chat_prefer_minutes. Without it a stop waited the hour every chat's own work waits before any AI could take it (2026-10-10, h_02fd5a223bb0e1e260ab7cf4).

chat_job: This chat ({source_id}) stopped because of {reason} at {stopped_at}, and nobody started it again. Carry on the work it was doing: read the end of its transcript ({transcript}) first, check what already landed (git log, its handoffs), and never redo landed work. {lanes_line}{queued_line}Do the work through to a checked result, then finish_work.
chat_lanes_line: Its stopped helper AIs ({lanes}) were each handed out separately through Trillion to the person's own AIs, so other chats and this computer's worker take them a few at a time; do not relaunch them from here (one chat relaunching about 80 helpers once filled this computer's memory).
chat_said: Carry on a chat that stopped because of {reason}
lane_said: Carry on the work of {lane}, which stopped because of {reason}
queued_line: {queued_messages} messages sent to it are still waiting unread; read them in its transcript and act on them.
stuck_job: This chat ({source_id}) is still open. It has been {reason} since {stopped_at}; only the person can answer that prompt on this computer, so the chat will not go on by itself. Carry on the work it was doing: read the end of its transcript ({transcript}) first, check what already landed (git log, its handoffs), and never redo landed work. {queued_line}Do the work through to a checked result, then finish_work.
